title: Weather Is Today; Climate Is the Pattern
description: A rainy Tuesday is weather. Thirty years of rainy Tuesdays is climate — and keeping the two apart clears up a lot of confusion.

body.heading: Two different questions
paragraphs: Weather is what the atmosphere is doing right now and over the next few days: this storm, this heatwave, this frost. It is changeable, local and sometimes chaotic.
Climate is the long-term pattern — the average of weather over decades, conventionally thirty years, along with how much it varies. One describes the moment; the other describes the habit.

body.heading: Why one cold day proves nothing
paragraphs: Because climate is statistics, a single event — one snowy week, one hot summer — is a data point, not a verdict. A team can lose one match and still be having a winning season.
A useful saying sums it up: weather is what you get, climate is what you expect. You dress for the weather, but you choose your wardrobe for the climate.

body.heading: How scientists keep the record
paragraphs: Climate records blend thermometer measurements going back more than a century with satellites, ocean buoys, tree rings and ice cores, each checking the others.
With records that long, patterns stand out from the noise — and slow changes that no single season could reveal become visible.

takeaway: Weather is what you get today; climate is what you expect over decades — one is a moment, the other is the pattern the moments make.
